Cheapie Bible

Hunter is 'King' of the SuperCoach NBL cap savers

Written By

Peter Brown

Senior Editor

Hunter Goodrick of the Sydney Kings poses with the NBL championship trophy after winning Game 5 of the NBL Grand Final series against the Adelaide 36ers at Qudos Bank Arena in Sydney on April 5, 2026. Photo: Darrian Traynor/Getty Images.

Share now:

Featured

Goodrick sits in 40 per cent of teams at $69,000. Narkle costs the same and 2.6 per cent own him.

  • ‍Ultimate Guide to mastering SuperCoach NBL Classic‍
  • Middle management: Blitz will unearth bargains‍
  • Bryce Cotton takes 23.7% of your cap. There's a wrinkle
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:55
Instaread

South East Melbourne big man and Sydney Kings NBL26 champion Hunter Goodrick ($69,000) is undeniably the best SuperCoach NBL Cheapie, already snapped up about 40% of SuperCoaches.

Goodrick, 26, is the backup power forward on the Phoenix behind import Yannis Morin ($277,000) on our depth chart but is a dual-position FWD/CTR at a rock-bottom price.

Two-position Cheapies are gold dust, especially one who, in just 7.8 minutes per game for the Sydney Kings last season, averaged 5.79 SC points. Goodrick is an unlikely SuperCoach NBL starter, but solid, reliable production at a great price for a player whose minutes are going to go up.

Illawarra Hawks second-year man Johny Narkle ($69,000) is most definitely one to put on your Watch List during the NBL27 Blitz. The NBL1 star is also a dual-position GRD/FWD, and our depth chart has him in the second-string behind Australian Tyler Harvey ($271,700) at shooting guard.

Whether that means minutes given to William Hickey ($331,600) could come off the bench, a la NBL25 Championship glory, and moving new import point guard Milton Doyle ($274,700) off the ball is anyone’s guess. He’s not on many radars, owned by just 2.6% of SuperCoaches, but with an average of 5.56 SC points in 7.7 minutes per game, maybe he should be.

Cairns veteran Shaun Bruce ($76,500) was the third-string point guard behind import Jaylon Brown ($277,000) and NBL Next Star Luke Paul ($115,000), who is out six to eight weeks with an ankle. Bruce, 35, becomes a viable option on the back of 7.37 SC points in 8.6 minutes last season for the Kings. That’s a decent amount of production for a man barely on the floor, and for the opening month of NBL27, he’s next man up for Adam Forde.

Another veteran back-up big with dual position benefits is Adelaide's Matt Kenyon ($69,000).

He's second-string small forward, but the man above him is Bul Kuol ($156,100), who is recovering from an ACL. Kenyon played all 40 games last year and averaged 5.42 SC points in 10.4 minutes a night. A dual-position FWD/GRD at the floor price who has never missed a game, owned by just 4.5% of coaches. We’ll need to wait and see what new head coach Trevor Gleeson does with his starting line – could it be: Bryce Cotton ($473,900), Flynn Cameron ($241,700), Zylan Cheatham ($339,500), Nick Rakocevic ($188,400) and Isaac Humphries ($265,300)?

Filter the list below to see the 13 “Cheapies” basketball.com.au has identified as having the potential to not only save cap space but actually contribute to your points total.

Ranked by value, a projected-minutes model over price. It is not a SuperCoach figure and not a prediction of scoring. Prices, player ids and ownership resolved against the live SuperCoach production API at 8:57am AEST, 2 September 2026; per-36 rates recomputed from the NBL26 season feed at the same time.
Per-36 is a rate, not a projection. It answers what a player did while he was on the floor, which is the only fair way to compare a man who played 45 minutes with one who played 600. None of these players is projected to play 36 minutes. Cameron Huefner carries a thin-sample badge. His per-36 rests on 45 minutes of court time, an extrapolation by a factor of about 48, so it is not comparable with rates built from hundreds of minutes. He is ranked on the depth chart, not on that rate.
Every name links to that player’s SuperCoach profile. The number in each link is resolved at build time from the player’s permanent key, because SuperCoach ids are positions in a list that re-sequences whenever the list grows — 126 of 136 moved between 11:11 and 15:52 on 31 August. Depth-chart reads and the one-line cases are editorial judgement, not data.
Four more cheapies have no NBL26 sample at all and carry no per-36 or value score. They are in a separate table, Block B: projected.

SuperCoach NBL27 cheapies — Block B: projected

Four players with no NBL26 sample at all · all at $69,000 · ranked on the path, not on a number

P1 | Anzac Rissetto NZL$69,0001.1723 games, 2 seasons, NBL22 and NBL23No NBL26 sample. Played in Germany with Phoenix Hagen2nd of only 2 at C (Bediako IP / Rissetto)Centre is the scarce position in this game, only 17 players carry it as a primary, and you need two. New Zealand carry exactly two
P2 | Ben Griscti ADL$69,0000.737 games, 1 season, NBL25No NBL26 sample2nd of only 2 at C (Humphries / Griscti)The same argument as Rissetto with less evidence behind it. Adelaide carry no third centre, so Isaac Humphries' rest minutes are his
P3 | Preston Le Gassick NZL$69,0004.13None. NBL debutantNo NBL26 sample. Arrived from Palm Beach Atlantic University, NCAA Division II2nd at PG (Jackson-Cartwright IP / Le Gassick / Evans Jr DP)Backup point guard to an import, at 4.13 per cent ownership. A pure projection, and his row says so
P4 | Ben Gold TAS$69,0006.06None. NBL debutantNo NBL26 sample. Arrived from Marquette, NCAA2nd at C (Magnay / Gold / Richardson DP), and Will Magnay's availability is unconfirmed6.06 per cent already own him, which is high for a debutant, and the man above him is the least certain starter in the league
There is no per-36 and no value score in this table, and that is deliberate. None of these four played an NBL minute in NBL26, so there is nothing to compute a rate from. Block A’s analytic columns are not repeated here with blanks in them: an empty cell beside Block A’s 26.2 reads as a low score rather than as an absence, and two different measurements must never share a column.
They are not rookies. Each is an experienced senior player who spent NBL26 somewhere other than the NBL, or is arriving from college, and each has walked into a top-two depth-chart slot. The ranking is P1 to P4 on the strength of that path, so it can never be read as a continuation of Block A’s 1 to 13.
Prices, ids and ownership resolved against the live SuperCoach production API at 8:57am AEST, 2 September 2026. Depth-chart reads and the one-line cases are editorial judgement, not data. The thirteen cheapies who DO have a measured NBL26 sample are in Block A: measured.
